chapter: Clarence Williams's 1936 article and the dispute
title: Williams's November 1936 letter correcting 'same' to 'similar' Tiger Rag
summary: The interviewer reads Williams's letter to the editor softening his claim about Tiger Rag.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You want me to read this now?
I want you to read that there.

This is from Orchestra World. Well, November 1936, letters to the editor. For the record, gentlemen, there is a correction I would like to make in the interview with me appearing in the October issue. In the third paragraph of the article, From Honky Tonk to Swing, I stated that I heard the same tune now called Tiger Rag when I was six or eight years old. Instead of the word same, I meant to say that the tune was somewhat similar to Tiger Rag. Mr. Williams has quoted same, and has put the word same in quotes, and has put the word similar in quotes. So it reads, instead of the word same, I mean to say the tune was somewhat similar to Tiger Rag. I would appreciate this correction very much, but it is not my intention to discredit Mr. Perrin Nick, Perrin Baraka as a composer of Tiger Rag, Clarence Williams Music Publishing Company, Inc. Perrin Baraka.
